stats.fact: OKF Agent Memory performs concept search in under 300 microseconds using in-memory BM25, vs 150–800ms for LLM/vector-DB runtimes like Mem0 and Letta.
Full corpus parse and graph validation takes ~4ms for 50+ concepts with zero external dependencies (single Go binary, <15MB RSS).
Retrieval cost: $0.00 per 1,000 queries (fully local BM25), vs ~$0.10–$0.50 for embedding-API-based memory.
OKF Agent Memory is git-native: all memory is version-controlled plain text, auditable with standard git diff and git log.
OKF v0.2 is Google's Open Knowledge Format spec hosted in the GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog repository.
OKF Agent Memory project created 2026-09-05, ~612 GitHub stars, Go language, MIT license.
Letta 'Context Repositories' stores agent context as git-backed local files, versioning every memory change with informative git commits.
HN: 'OKF Agent Memory — Git-native persistent memory' drew ~80 points and 32 comments; 'MCP Memory using OKF + SQLite FTS5' drew 70 points / 36 comments.

angles: The 'forgetting crisis': coding agents reset every session — git-native memory lets decisions, architecture and operational facts survive context windows as versioned plain text.
Zero-vendor-lock, zero-API-cost memory: in-memory BM25 (<300µs) replaces embedding backends, with git diff/log as the audit trail instead of a black-box vector DB.
Search-before-write and progressive disclosure: avoid context bloat and concept duplication by loading only the exact knowledge an agent needs.
The ecosystem race: Letta's context repositories vs OKF's standard vs grep-style tools (Darc) — four competing designs for how agents remember.
Governance: bind architecture decisions to source via code_refs and enforce holds with --for-path, turning memory into an enforceable engineering control.
Convergent evolution on 'memory as plain files': Markdown + YAML + git is the pragmatic middle ground between ad-hoc AGENTS.md and complex RAG.
